_comment: A grip beside a close neighbour stays grabbable: two Infantry regiments (60 men each, 11 files at an 18 wu, 0.9 m pitch; drill mode, no opponent) stand side by side facing south, the left centred at (700, 500) and the right at (904, 500), so their facing flank men are only 24 wu apart. The left one is clicked to select it; its east grip sits at x = 804.5 (700 + 90 half-width + 4.5 body radius + 10 handle gap), inside the right regiment's padded pick box (which reaches x = 803.5) but outside its men and block (which start at x = 809.5). The grip is grabbed there and dragged two pitches west, and the left regiment narrows to 9 files from its fixed west edge, while the right one is untouched. Before the fix, any neighbour's pick box under the press took the click, so this press selected the right regiment instead. Finally a click on one of the right regiment's men selects it. Driven live through the real SelectionManager by tools/demo/DemoInputRecorder.gd; world coordinates; physics ticks (60/s).
